claims.title: Four-character product, entire continuation, near-one upper bound, alternating Taylor series at s = 2, and the Estermann key inequality
claims.hypotheses: Positive moduli q₁, q₂ ≥ 1 and real quadratic nonprincipal Dirichlet characters χ₁ modulo q₁ and χ₂ modulo q₂ (χ₁² = χ₂² = 1, χ₁ ≠ 1, χ₂ ≠ 1), together with a nonprincipal product character ψ modulo q₁q₂ satisfying ψ(n) = χ₁(n)χ₂(n) for every natural number n; the polynomial growth bound for ζ in Re s > 0 from DZF-01 and the partial-summation polynomial growth bound for nonprincipal L-functions in Re s ≥ 1/2 from LZE-02; and a real parameter σ ∈ [7/8, 1).
claims.statement: For Re s > 1, the product F(s) = ζ(s) L(s, χ₁) L(s, χ₂) L(s, ψ) equals a Dirichlet series ∑ aₙ n^{−s} with a₁ = 1, aₙ ≥ 0 for all n, and abscissa of absolute convergence at most 1; subtracting the pole term λ/(s − 1), where λ = L(1, χ₁) L(1, χ₂) L(1, ψ), extends F(s) − λ/(s − 1) to an entire function G(s). On the circle |s − 2| = 3/2, |F(s)| ≤ C_g (q₁q₂)³ with C_g = 14(9|C_G|/2)³, where C_G is the growth constant for nonprincipal L-functions in Re s ≥ 1/2. For every nonprincipal χ modulo q ≥ 1 and every complex w with Re w ≥ 1 − 3/(2 log(3q)), Re w ≥ 1/4, and |w| ≤ 2, one has |L(w, χ)| ≤ C_L log(3q) with C_L = 38 e^{3/2}, and in particular |L(1, χ)| ≤ 38 e^{3/2} log(3q). Consequently there exist absolute real constants C_B and K ≥ 0 (explicitly K = max(K_g, 2)/log(4/3) = 3/log(4/3) and C_B = e² exp(log(8c₀)/(8 log(4/3))) with c₀ = |C_g| + 54|C_L|³ + 1) such that for all such (χ₁, χ₂, ψ) and all σ ∈ [7/8, 1), 1/2 − C_B |λ| (q₁q₂)^{K(1−σ)} / (1 − σ) ≤ Re F(σ).
definitions: product character relation ψ(n) = χ₁(n)χ₂(n) modulo q₁q₂, four-character product F(s) = ζ(s) L(s, χ₁) L(s, χ₂) L(s, ψ), and residue λ = L(1, χ₁) L(1, χ₂) L(1, ψ)
entire regularized function G(s) = F(s) − λ/(s − 1) and circle supremum bound B = c₀ (q₁q₂)^{K′} on |s − 2| = 3/2
Taylor coefficients βₙ = ((−1)ⁿ/n!) F^{(n)}(2) ≥ 0 with β₀ = F(2) ≥ 1, and truncation order M = ⌈log(8B)/log(4/3)⌉ + 1

claims.correspondence: Prime-power nonnegativity of the multiplicative convolution (1 ∗ χ₁) ∗ (χ₂ ∗ ψ) holds by swapping χ₁, χ₂ unless χ₁(p) = χ₂(p) = −1, where the alternating sum vanishes for odd exponents and equals 1 for even exponents. Subtracting λ/(s − 1) uses the entire function ζ(s) − 1/(s − 1) (value γ at 1) plus the divided difference of L(·, χ₁)L(·, χ₂)L(·, ψ) at 1. Expanding G about s = 2 cancels the simple pole term +λ/(1 − σ) against the geometric sum −λ((x^M − 1)/(x − 1)) for x = 2 − σ ∈ (1, 9/8], leaving 1 − |λ|(2 − σ)^M/(1 − σ) − 4B(3/4)^M ≤ Re F(σ); choosing M = ⌈log(8B)/log(4/3)⌉ + 1 makes 4B(3/4)^M ≤ 1/2 and bounds (2 − σ)^M via 2 − σ ≤ exp(1 − σ).
claims.review: Checked prime-power convolution cases, |ζ(s)| ≤ 14 on |s − 2| = 3/2 (Re s ≥ 1/2, |s| ≤ 7/2, |s − 1| ≥ 1/2), near-one partial sum e^{3/2}(1 + log(3q)) plus endpoint e^{3/2} and tail 8 e^{3/2} ≤ 38 e^{3/2} log(3q), alternating derivatives (−1)^m (s − 1)^{-1}|_{s=2} = m!, Cauchy tail 4B(3/4)^M from x/(3/2) ≤ 3/4, and the truncation order M ≤ log(8B)/log(4/3) + 2.

claims.title: Character existence, real-line sign control, same-character Euler-factor comparison, and Estermann–Landau deduction of Siegel’s lower bound
claims.hypotheses: A positive real exponent ε > 0; the Estermann key inequality (constants C_B and K ≥ 0) and the uniform bound |L(1, χ)| ≤ C_L log(3q) from SCB-01; and the telescoping representation (s − 1)ζ(s) = s − D(s) in Re s > 0 from DZF-01.
claims.statement: There exists c > 0 (depending only on ε) such that |L(1, χ)| ≥ c q^{−ε} for every modulus q ≥ 1 and every real quadratic nonprincipal Dirichlet character χ modulo q (χ² = 1, χ ≠ 1). Along the way: every pair (χ₁, χ₂) modulo (q₁, q₂) induces a product character ψ modulo q₁q₂, and the nonprincipal quadratic character modulo 4 exists; ζ(σ) is real and strictly negative for all σ ∈ (0, 1); for a real nonprincipal χ, L(σ, χ) is real and strictly positive on [σ₀, ∞) whenever L(·, χ) has no zeros there; and whenever nonprincipal characters χ₁ modulo q₁ and χ modulo q agree on all integers coprime to q₁q, |L(1, χ₁)| ≤ (ω(q₁q) + 1)² |L(1, χ)|, where ω(n) counts the distinct prime factors of n.
definitions: threshold exponent σ₀ = max(7/8, 1 − ε/(2(K + 1))) ∈ [7/8, 1), satisfying K(1 − σ) ≤ ε/2 on [σ₀, 1)
distinct prime-factor count ω(n) and elementary bound (ω(n) + 1)² ≤ (2/(ε log 2) + 1)² n^ε from 2^{ω(n)} ≤ n
unified Siegel constant c = min((1 − σ)/(2 max(C_B, 1) |L(1, χ₁)| (|C_L| + 1) (2/ε) (3q₁)^ε), |L(1, χ₁)|/((2/(ε log 2) + 1)² (3q₁)^ε)) for a fixed pair (χ₁, σ) with Re F(σ) ≤ 0

claims.correspondence: In Case 1 some real nonprincipal χ₁ has a real zero β ∈ [σ₀, 1), so F(β) = 0 and Re F(β) ≤ 0; in Case 2 no real nonprincipal character vanishes on [σ₀, 1), so taking χ₁ to be the nonprincipal character modulo 4 and evaluating at σ₀ gives ζ(σ₀) < 0 while L(σ₀, χ₁), L(σ₀, χ), L(σ₀, ψ) > 0, forcing Re F(σ₀) < 0 ≤ 0. Both cases feed into the same product-character inequality: when ψ = 1, χ₁ and χ agree on units modulo q₁q and the Euler-factor comparison bounds |L(1, χ₁)|/|L(1, χ)| ≤ (ω(q₁q) + 1)²; when ψ ≠ 1, Re F(σ) ≤ 0 in the Estermann key inequality bounds |L(1, χ)| from below using |L(1, ψ)| ≤ (|C_L| + 1)(3q₁q)^{ε/2}/(ε/2) and (q₁q)^{K(1−σ)} ≤ (3q₁q)^{ε/2}.
claims.review: Checked ζ(σ) = σ/(σ − 1) − ∑ rₙ < 0 with rₙ = ∫_{n+1}^{n+2} (x^{−σ} − (n+2)^{−σ}) dx ≥ 0, Schwarz conjugation and intermediate value theorem from L(σ, χ) → 1 as σ → ∞, induction on finite prime sets for ∏(1 − 1/p) ≥ 1/(|S| + 1) and (1 + 1/p)(1 − 1/p) ≤ 1, 2^{ω(n)} ≤ n giving (ω(n) + 1)² ≤ (2/(ε log 2) + 1)² n^ε, and exact Case 1 and Case 2 specialization of the unified product-character theorem.

claims.title: Cauchy first-derivative bound near s = 1 and deduction of the exceptional-zero gap
claims.hypotheses: Modulus q ≥ 1 and nonprincipal Dirichlet character χ modulo q (so q ≥ 3 and log(3q) ≥ 2); the near-one bound |L(w, χ)| ≤ 38 e^{3/2} log(3q) for Re w ≥ 1 − 3/(2 log(3q)), Re w ≥ 1/4, |w| ≤ 2 from SCB-01; and Siegel’s lower bound |L(1, χ)| ≥ c₀ q^{−ε/3} for real nonprincipal characters from SCB-02.
claims.statement: For every q ≥ 1, every nonprincipal character χ modulo q, and every real σ ∈ [1 − 1/log(3q), 1], one has |L′(σ, χ)| ≤ 76 e^{3/2} (log(3q))². Consequently, for every ε > 0 there exists c > 0 such that for every q ≥ 1, every real quadratic nonprincipal character χ modulo q (χ² = 1, χ ≠ 1), and every real β with L(β, χ) = 0, one has β ≤ 1 − c q^{−ε}.
definitions: Cauchy circle |z − σ| = 1/(2 log(3q)) about σ ∈ [1 − 1/log(3q), 1], lying in Re z ≥ 1 − 3/(2 log(3q)), Re z ≥ 1/4, and |z| ≤ 2
logarithmic power-absorption constant K_ε = log 3 + 3/ε satisfying log(3q) ≤ K_ε q^{ε/3} for all q ≥ 1
exceptional-zero gap constant c = min(1/K_ε, c₀/(M_D K_ε²)) with M_D = max(C_D, 1), C_D = 76 e^{3/2}, and c₀ from Siegel’s lower bound at exponent ε/3

claims.correspondence: On the circle |z − σ| = 1/(2 log(3q)) around σ ∈ [1 − 1/log(3q), 1], log(3q) ≥ 2 ensures 1/log(3q) ≤ 1/2, 1/(2 log(3q)) ≤ 1/4, Re z ≥ 1 − 3/(2 log(3q)) ≥ 1/4, and |z| ≤ 5/4 ≤ 2, so Cauchy’s estimate divides 38 e^{3/2} log(3q) by 1/(2 log(3q)) to give 76 e^{3/2} (log(3q))². For a real zero β < 1 of a real nonprincipal χ, if β ≤ 1 − 1/log(3q) then 1 − β ≥ 1/log(3q) ≥ (1/K) q^{−ε/3} ≥ c q^{−ε}; otherwise the mean-value inequality on [β, 1] gives c₀ q^{−ε/3} ≤ |L(1, χ) − L(β, χ)| ≤ M K² q^{2ε/3}(1 − β), whence 1 − β ≥ (c₀/(M K²)) q^{−ε} ≥ c q^{−ε}.
claims.review: Checked q ≥ 3 for nonprincipal χ, log 9 > 2 from e < 2.72, circle geometry 1/log(3q) + 1/(2 log(3q)) = 3/(2 log(3q)), 38 · 2 = 76, log(3q) ≤ (log 3 + 3/ε) q^{ε/3}, u = q^{ε/3} ≥ 1 ⇒ u ≤ u³, and both branches of the mean-value inequality with c = min(1/K, c₀/(M K²)).

outstanding: The constants c(ε) in Siegel’s lower bound and the exceptional-zero gap are ineffective because Case 1 selects a hypothetical real zero β ≥ σ₀ depending on ε; the progression and mean-square estimates in ETZ-03, SMR-02, PSR-01, and PRE-01 consume the resulting gap at fixed exponents ε = 1 and ε = 1/2.
